limitations: The bike and the park notice board are invented portfolio fixtures generated at bench scale and placed by world rect; the master paints neither.

Both foreground trees and the marquee bulb string are measured mattes of the master (radial colour trace, hand-measured band): their cut-outs carry a thin halo of the surrounding plate pixels, invisible at rest because they sit on identical pixels.
The Eads deck rect is axis aligned over a sloping deck: it reaches the east bank at every row it covers, so it also excludes a wedge of water north of the deck from the river mask.

Codex redrew rather than registered the trees, the bulb string, the Eads Bridge (larger and over the Arch) and the first MonsterCommerce sign attempt; the sign was accepted on a tighter 3:2 crop, the other four are measured mattes.
The Eads Bridge matte carries the deck, abutments and piers only; the steel arches stay in the plate, so a cursor in the river north of the deck draws over them.
District rects are separated by 10 to 20 px rather than the spec's "about 200 px": on this master the West End row sits directly above SLU, so the sound-bed footprints only just clear each other.
The Forest Park sign is painted in the plate only; the spec has no scene-data type for a strip sign.

The Codex CLI's built-in image tool is fixed to gpt-image-2 at automatic quality; the gpt-image-2.5 Sunburst pass at max quality (art/sources/overworld-fix/run-api.sh) has not been run because no OPENAI_API_KEY is set on this machine.

Tile fixes are the model's redraw accepted only inside the marked loops (0.7 px feather), the Eads deck band and the lake shore band; the lake's outline and loop path are the model's line inside that band, the deck's underside girder is the model's along its whole length, and where a footpath crosses a band edge the join can step by a pixel or two. Deleted trees are refilled lawn: at 4x a faint lighter patch can be seen where a tree stood on shaded lawn. The boat house keeps its base pixels, so the model's grass verge meets its west wall at a straight edge.
